title: Polite decline email
prompt:
Write an email to Jordan at Lumen Analytics declining their proposal for a customer-churn
dashboard. Facts to use: our budget for new tools is frozen until the next fiscal year,
which starts in July; we liked their demo; we would be open to talking again in June.
Keep it under 120 words, warm but direct, and do not apologize for the decision.
system:
You are completing one task from an evaluation suite. Do the task as asked.

Reply with the requested text only, with no preamble about what you are doing.

rubric.name: clear_decline
rubric.description: Clearly says no to the proposal for now. The reader cannot mistake it for a maybe.

rubric.name: reason_and_reopen
rubric.description: Gives the real reason (budget frozen until the fiscal year that starts in July) and offers to talk again in June.

rubric.name: tone
rubric.description: Warm and direct, mentions that the demo was liked, and does not apologize for the decision.

rubric.name: length
rubric.description: Under 120 words, and reads as a complete email with a greeting and sign-off.

reference:
Subject: Lumen proposal

Hi Jordan,

Thank you for the proposal and for the demo. The team was impressed by how quickly the
churn dashboard surfaced at-risk accounts.

We have decided not to move forward right now. Our budget for new tools is frozen until
the next fiscal year begins in July, so we cannot take on a new contract before then.

I would be glad to pick this up again in June, when planning for the new year is under
way. If that works for you, I will reach out then to set up a call.

Best regards,
Sam
answers:
